title: Put a five-piece wooden matryoshka back together, pressing each snug top onto its own bottom with its face lined up
instruction: Put the nesting dolls back together, each one closed and facing the same way as its body, with the smaller ones inside the largest.
context: Putting a nesting doll set back together after it has been played with is something most people have done. Each top is turned to a snug fit over a collar on its own bottom half: set on its collar it stops several millimetres up, and it closes only when pressed square (here about 10 N for the largest), so the dolls must be closed one by one, the smallest first, each with its face over its apron.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y left; heights from the table top). One fixed layout, as in the screenshot. A five-piece turned linden (lime) matryoshka, lacquered red with a gold shawl, a painted face on each top and a cream apron on each bottom half, the face and apron on the half's same side. Doll 1: 150 mm tall, 71 mm across, split 62 mm up; bottom half 32 g, standing open end up at x 240, y 25, apron toward the arms; top 20 g, standing on its rim at x 215, y 200, its face turned a quarter turn to the right of the apron's direction (facing the right arm). Doll 2: 103.5 mm by 49 mm, split 42.8 mm up; bottom 13 g at x 230, y -105, apron toward the arms; top 8 g at x 355, y -190, its face a quarter turn to the left (facing the left arm). Doll 3: 63 mm by 30 mm, closed with dolls 4 and 5 inside (10 g together), standing at x 190, y -215. Walls 3.5 mm (doll 1) and 3 mm (doll 2); floors 5 and 4 mm. Each bottom half has a collar (spigot) 10 mm (doll 1) or 8 mm (doll 2) tall above its shoulder; its top's bore is a snug friction fit over it. Distractors, ignored by scoring: a white pillar candle (74 mm across, 75 mm tall, 350 g) at x 530, y 230; a ceramic mug (about 12 cm with its handle, 300 g) at x 540, y -30; a metal ballpoint pen (160 mm, 20 g) at x 470, y -300.
scoring: Read at the end from the video and photos (opening the set afterwards to confirm what is inside). Seated: a top's rim within 1 mm of its bottom's shoulder (no gap), centred within 1.5 mm and square within 3 degrees. Facing: the top's face within 15 degrees of the apron below it. Inside: a doll standing on the floor of the next bottom half, within 2 mm of it, 10 mm of its axis and 8 degrees of upright. 0.25: doll 3 inside doll 2's bottom half. 0.5: that, and doll 2's own top seated and facing. 0.75: that, and the closed doll 2 inside doll 1's bottom half. 1.0: that, and doll 1's own top seated and facing, doll 1 standing on the table (within 2 mm, upright within 5 degrees), every gripper fingertip at least 30 mm from every piece, and no piece moving more than 1 mm or 1 degree, all held for 1 s. 0 for anything else, and 0 for the trial if any piece falls off the table (ends more than 30 mm below its top) at any time.
reset_notes: Open dolls 1 and 2 (doll 3 stays closed with 4 and 5 inside) and stand the halves on tape marks, faces turned as listed; check each top still rests 5-7 mm up when set on its collar unpressed.
fidelity: Rigid turned shells at the listed sizes, colliders as convex pieces; masses from linden at 500 kg/m3. The snug fit is four hidden sprung pads per collar standing 0.6/0.5 mm proud of the bore, gripping it by contact friction (0.5/0.4): unpressed a top rests 6.9/5.1 mm up; a square push seats it at about 10/5 N; it pulls off at about 9/4 N. Doll 3 with dolls 4-5 inside is one closed body. Paint is visual; no wood compliance beyond the pads.
